It won the ~$400M An-32RE upgrade in 2009 (40 in Ukraine + 64 at Kanpur), but the programme stalled after 2014–15 as Russia-Ukraine tensions and, later, the war crippled its supply chain and OEM support.

what_it_is.prose: Antonov State Enterprise is Ukraine's state aircraft design house and manufacturer (part of the Ukroboronprom state defence conglomerate), and is the original design authority and OEM for the Antonov An-32 — the Indian Air Force's medium-transport workhorse, of which the IAF operates roughly 100 or more airframes inducted from 1984. In 2009 Antonov won a roughly $400 million contract to upgrade the IAF fleet to the 'An-32RE' standard, with about 40 aircraft to be upgraded in Ukraine and a further ~64 at the IAF's No. 1 Base Repair Depot in Kanpur under transfer of technology; the first RE aircraft entered service around 2011. The programme then stalled: strained Russia-Ukraine ties after the 2014 annexation of Crimea, Antonov's own supply-chain and financial difficulties, and ultimately the full-scale Russia-Ukraine war disrupted OEM support, spares and engine supply, leaving the upgrade incomplete and pushing India toward an indigenous overhaul and life-extension route. Antonov (and the parent Ukroboronprom) subsequently pitched other aircraft to India — including An-132 co-production and the An-178 — but these were not adopted at scale. Antonov thus remains a strategically important but war-impaired foreign OEM dependency for a core IAF airlift fleet.

import_dependencies.summary: Antonov itself is the foreign (Ukraine) dependency: as design authority and OEM for the An-32 it controls airframe support, RE-standard kits and the Ivchenko-Progress AI-20 engine ecosystem — all disrupted by the Russia-Ukraine war, which is precisely why India pivoted to indigenous overhaul.

faq.question: What is Antonov's relationship to the Indian Air Force?
faq.answer: Antonov State Enterprise (Ukraine) is the original design authority and OEM for the Antonov An-32, the IAF's medium-transport workhorse (~100+ aircraft from 1984). In 2009 Antonov won a ~$400 million contract to upgrade the fleet to An-32RE standard — about 40 aircraft in Ukraine and 64 at No. 1 BRD Kanpur under transfer of technology.

faq.question: Why did the Antonov An-32 upgrade stall?
faq.answer: After strained Russia-Ukraine ties following the 2014 annexation of Crimea, Antonov's own supply-chain and financial difficulties, and later the full-scale war, OEM support, spares and engine supply were disrupted. The RE upgrade was left incomplete, and India shifted toward an indigenous overhaul and life-extension route at Kanpur BRD.
